ak-frontend-design.tagline: Build polished UI from prompts, screenshots, videos, or components.
ak-frontend-design.summary: ak:frontend-design turns a prompt, image/video path, or component into runnable UI code on the project's real stack, with responsive layout, accessible controls, and full interaction states. It picks a design contract first and underpins ak:show-off and the ak:stitch handoff.
howItWorks: Picks a design contract: improve existing UI, replicate screenshot/video, describe only, new UI, 3D/WebGL, quick, or immersive.
For replication, ak:ai-multimodal extracts fonts, colors, radius, spacing, and shadows; ak:ui-ux-pro-max is activated.
The ui-ux-designer subagent writes plan.md and phases, then implements them on the real stack and design system.
Uses real content, all interaction states, and accessible controls; never invents stats or testimonials.
Checks rendering at mobile and desktop sizes, build, and tests; reports unverified parts honestly.
useWhen: You have a UI screenshot or video and want an exact replica.
You need a new landing page or component with its own art direction.
You want a quick prototype or an immersive 3D/WebGL experience.
avoidWhen: Mostly React/TypeScript logic, data fetching, or routing: use ak-frontend-development.
Only a shadcn component or Tailwind theme tweak: use ak-ui-styling.
Logo, banner, or brand identity: use ak-design.

params.name: [prompt|image-path|component]
params.desc: UI prompt, image/video path to replicate, or component to improve; determines the design contract.

examples.note: Replicate a dashboard from a screenshot.

examples.cmd: /ak:frontend-design landing page for a meditation app, warm minimalist style

examples.note: Improve an existing component, keeping current tokens.

tips: When replicating, identify the actual font; avoid defaulting to Inter or Poppins.
With no framework specified, the screenshot workflow defaults to HTML/CSS/JS.
Generate image assets with ak:ai-multimodal and process them with ak:media-processing.

ak-frontend-development.tagline: Implement React/TypeScript frontends with modern patterns on your stack.
ak-frontend-development.summary: ak:frontend-development builds React/TS components, data fetching, routing, and loading/error states, verified in the real router with build and types passing. It respects the existing stack and never installs MUI or TanStack Router into a project that lacks them.
howItWorks: Inspects package manifest, router/data libraries, conventions, aliases, and styling before editing.
Implements typed boundaries, accessible controls, correct hooks, effect cleanup, and loading/error/empty states.
Uses references/stack-recipes.md only if the project already uses MUI/TanStack.
Tests in the real router, verifies build and types, and reports untested runtime behavior.
useWhen: Writing a new React/TypeScript component that follows project conventions.
Adding Suspense/useSuspenseQuery data fetching where TanStack Query already exists.
Setting up routes, lazy loading, and loading/error boundaries.
avoidWhen: Visual fidelity is the focus: use ak-frontend-design.
Measured React/Next.js performance problem: use ak-react-best-practices.
Next.js App Router, SSR, or Turborepo work: use ak-web-frameworks.

params.name: [component or feature]
params.desc: Frontend component or feature to implement or fix.

examples.note: Component with typed props and all states.

tips: Skill recipes for MUI/TanStack Router are examples only; do not add them to other stacks.
Choose memo/lazy by actual cost; do not memoize everything.
Clean up listeners, subscriptions, and timers in effects to avoid leaks.

ak-react-best-practices.tagline: 45 Vercel React/Next.js performance rules, ranked by impact.
ak-react-best-practices.summary: ak:react-best-practices applies Vercel's 45 React/Next.js performance rules in 8 priority groups, from waterfalls and bundle size to re-renders. Use it on a measured bottleneck to get a rule-based refactor with before/after metrics.
howItWorks: Starts from an observed bottleneck: profile, waterfall, bundle, or render.
Picks rules by prefix (async-, bundle-, rerender-, ...), reads each rules/ file, and checks version support.
Applies the change and compares metrics before and after; reads AGENTS.md only for broad audits.
useWhen: Request waterfalls in server components or API routes (async-parallel).
Bundles bloated by barrel imports or heavy libraries.
Excess re-renders measured with the profiler, or a pre-release performance review.
avoidWhen: No evidence of a performance problem: do not apply rules wholesale.
Building ordinary React features: use ak-frontend-development.
Next.js caching/SSR/ISR config: use ak-web-frameworks.

params.name: [component or pattern]
params.desc: Component, page, or pattern to optimize or review.

examples.note: Remove fetch waterfalls in a server component.
Broad audit; only then read AGENTS.md.

tips: CRITICAL groups (waterfalls, bundle size) usually pay off most; you need not apply every rule.
Some rules are version-specific (after(), Activity, React.cache()); check first.
Re-measure after every fix to prove the improvement.
artifacts: No new files; edits existing React/Next.js code

ak-ui-styling.tagline: Style UIs with shadcn/ui and Tailwind: components, themes, dark mode.
ak-ui-styling.summary: ak:ui-styling adds or edits shadcn/ui components, Tailwind config, themes, dark mode, and tokens. It inspects existing config and changes only what you ask, never re-initializing an existing app.
howItWorks: Inspects package versions, components.json, Tailwind config, and tokens.
Loads only the relevant shadcn/Tailwind/theming references; setup recipes only for new setup.
Runs scripts/shadcn_add.py or scripts/tailwind_config_gen.py as needed, preserving existing design and focus behavior.
useWhen: Adding shadcn components such as Dialog, Data Table, or Command palette.
Implementing dark mode with next-themes and CSS variables.
Customizing Tailwind tokens (@theme, colors, fonts, breakpoints).
avoidWhen: Art direction and high visual fidelity: use ak-frontend-design.
Style/palette/font choices or a UX review: use ak-ui-ux-pro-max.
React logic or data fetching: use ak-frontend-development.

params.name: [component or layout]
params.desc: Component or layout to add, style, or customize.

examples.cmd: /ak:ui-styling dark mode for the whole app

tips: Write full Tailwind class names; dynamic ones get purged.
Apply dark variants to every themed element.
Do not re-init shadcn when components.json exists; add only needed components.

ak-ui-ux-pro-max.tagline: Searchable UI/UX design intelligence plus guideline reviews of existing UI.
ak-ui-ux-pro-max.summary: ak:ui-ux-pro-max recommends design systems from a searchable database of styles, palettes, font pairings, product types, UX guidelines, and chart types, optionally saved as design-system/MASTER.md. It also reviews existing UI against its rules and Vercel's Web Interface Guidelines, reporting findings with file:line.
howItWorks: Analyzes product type, audience, style keywords, and stack from the request and existing code.
Runs scripts/search.py "<keywords>" --design-system for pattern, style, colors, typography, effects, and anti-patterns.
--persist writes design-system/MASTER.md; --page adds a page override that takes precedence over MASTER.
Reviews sweep 10 rule groups plus a fetched Web Interface Guidelines pass, recording its URL and revision.
Reports each finding with file:line, rule, impact, and fix; runs the pre-delivery checklist before handoff.
useWhen: Designing new pages or components, or choosing color, type, and spacing systems.
Reviewing UI code for accessibility, UX, and consistency.
The UI looks unprofessional for unclear reasons before launch.
avoidWhen: Backend, API, DevOps, or non-UI work.
Polished UI code straight from a screenshot or prompt: use ak-frontend-design.
Styling specific shadcn/Tailwind components only: use ak-ui-styling.

params.name: [component|page|design-system]
params.desc: Scope: one component, one page, or a full design system.

params.name: --style <style>
params.desc: Desired style, e.g. glassmorphism. Not in source; search.py's closest is --domain style "<keyword>".

params.name: --framework <fw>
params.desc: Target framework. Not in source; search.py uses --stack/-s instead.

params.name: --design-system (-ds)
params.desc: Generate a full design system; combine with -p/--project-name and -f/--format ascii|markdown (ascii default).

params.name: --persist
params.desc: Save to design-system/MASTER.md; --page <name> writes pages/<name>.md; -o/--output-dir changes location (default current dir).

params.name: --domain (-d) <domain>
params.desc: Search one domain (style, color, chart, landing, product, ux, typography, icons, react, web, google-fonts). -n defaults to 3; --json outputs JSON.

params.name: --stack (-s) <stack>
params.desc: Stack guidelines; --help currently accepts only react-native. Never force react-native onto web/Vue.

examples.cmd: python3 scripts/search.py "beauty spa wellness service" --design-system -p "Serenity Spa"
examples.note: Full design system for a new project.
Save MASTER.md plus a dashboard override.

examples.cmd: /ak:ui-ux-pro-max review src/app/settings for accessibility against Web Interface Guidelines
examples.note: Review existing UI; findings with file:line.

tips: Use multi-dimensional keywords (product + industry + tone + density), not just 'app'.
When building a page, read design-system/pages/<page>.md first, then MASTER.md.
Quick Reference sections: dark mode §6, animation §7, forms §8, navigation §9, small screens §5.
artifacts: Review findings with file:line, rule, impact, fix

ak-stitch.tagline: Generate UI designs with Google Stitch, export, and hand off to code.
ak-stitch.summary: ak:stitch generates high-fidelity UI designs from text prompts and exports HTML/Tailwind, a screenshot, and DESIGN.md for implementing skills. It needs STITCH_API_KEY, isolates projects per git repo, and tracks quota locally.
howItWorks: Checks STITCH_API_KEY without printing it and the local quota estimate; stops if the key is missing.
Generates with scripts/stitch-generate.ts, shows the image for feedback, and optionally makes variants.
Exports design.html, design.png, and DESIGN.md with stitch-export.ts --format all.
Hands off to ak:frontend-design, ak:ui-ux-pro-max, or ak:ui-styling, which auto-detect DESIGN.md.
useWhen: Exploring many UI design options quickly from a text description.
Prototyping a page before coding it.
You need DESIGN.md or HTML/Tailwind as a starting spec for implementation.
avoidWhen: No STITCH_API_KEY or quota exhausted: use ak-ui-ux-pro-max.
Exact replica of an existing screenshot: use ak-frontend-design.
Animation or direct React export: Stitch outputs static HTML/Tailwind only.

params.name: [design prompt or action]
params.desc: Design prompt, or an action: generate, export, quota, edit.

params.name: generate
params.desc: Generate a design from a prompt; returns a screen ID and preview image URL.

params.name: export
params.desc: Export a screen as HTML/Tailwind, image, and DESIGN.md.

params.name: quota
params.desc: check, increment, or reset the daily quota in ~/.claudekit/.stitch-quota.json; warns below 20%.

params.name: edit
params.desc: Refine an existing design via the SDK (screen.edit("...")).

params.name: --project <id>
params.desc: generate: direct Stitch project ID; highest priority.

params.name: --project-name <title>
params.desc: generate: find or create a project by name; falls back to STITCH_PROJECT_ID, git repo name, then 'claudekit-default'.

params.name: --device MOBILE|DESKTOP|TABLET
params.desc: generate: target device type.

params.name: --variants <count>
params.desc: generate: number of extra alternative designs.

params.name: --format html|image|all
params.desc: export: output format; all produces design.html, design.png, and DESIGN.md.

params.name: --output <dir>
params.desc: export: output directory (e.g. ./stitch-exports/).

examples.cmd: /ak:stitch A checkout page with payment form and cart summary
npx tsx scripts/stitch-generate.ts "mobile banking home" --device MOBILE --variants 2

tips: Keep STITCH_API_KEY in the environment or a secret store; scripts need Node (npx tsx).
The local quota count is an estimate, not the real account quota.
Output can be generic; pair it with an ak:ui-ux-pro-max style guide and add breakpoints.

ak-page-builder.tagline: Integrate, extend, or operate an agent-driven page builder.
ak-page-builder.summary: ak:page-builder adds a page builder to an existing project from its real components, with agents as primary operators and an accessible editor for humans. It runs in setup, update, or operate mode and creates a project-specific operator skill via ak-skill-creator.
howItWorks: Infers the mode from the request and project; explicit arguments win.
Discovers the host app, existing CMS/builder, components, auth/storage, and deployment, then picks an adapter.
Defines the block registry and page contract, wires the editor and preview/publish, and verifies one real block first.
Exposes API, CLI, MCP, WebMCP, and SEO/Markdown export; creates the operator skill (mandatory on setup).
Operate mode reads the operator skill, edits content through existing operations, then previews or publishes.
useWhen: Building a reusable page composition system from existing components.
Adding draft/preview/publish and agent operation to an existing builder.
Extending a builder with new blocks, bindings, or layouts.
avoidWhen: Designing a single page: use ak-frontend-design.
Wrapping an API as a generic CLI/MCP: use ak-agentize or ak-mcp-builder.
Routine content edits when an operator skill exists: use that skill.

params.name: setup
params.desc: Skill argument: integrate a new builder with registry, editor, draft/preview/publish, API, CLI, MCP, WebMCP, docs, SEO export, and an operator skill.

params.name: update
params.desc: Extend an existing builder (blocks, bindings, layouts, contracts); changes only affected behavior.

params.name: operate
params.desc: Edit content, preview, and publish through the operator skill; no source regeneration. Creates the operator skill if missing.

params.name: [project-path]
params.desc: Target app path (e.g. ./apps/storefront).

params.name: [request]
params.desc: The specific request (e.g. add a ProductGrid block with category bindings).

examples.cmd: /ak:page-builder update Add the existing ProductGrid block with category bindings
/ak:page-builder operate Create a pricing draft and share its preview
examples.note: Agent creates a draft and shares the preview.

tips: setup/update/operate are skill arguments, not ak CLI subcommands.
Draft, preview, queued deploy, and verified live publish differ; never claim publish without evidence.
Test mutations in a disposable environment; without credentials, live verification is incomplete.
artifacts: Page builder code (registry, editor, operations, preview/publish)
API, CLI, MCP server, WebMCP tools, OpenAPI docs
Plan in plans/ for new integrations

ak-threejs.tagline: Build 3D web experiences with Three.js: WebGL/WebGPU, GLTF, physics, XR.
ak-threejs.summary: ak:threejs builds Three.js scenes using a CLI that searches bundled examples and API data, with references from fundamentals to WebGPU, physics, and XR. Output is working 3D code checked for real rendering and interaction.
howItWorks: Reads the Three.js version and renderer first; WebGL, WebGPU, and TSL recipes differ.
Searches examples and APIs with python3 scripts/search.py, loading references from fundamentals to XR/WebGPU.
Verifies add-on imports and real rendering; disposes GPU resources on teardown.
useWhen: Building a 3D product configurator with GLTF, PBR, and env maps.
Making a game, 3D data visualization, panorama, or WebXR experience.
Adding particles, postprocessing, or WebGPU compute shaders.
avoidWhen: Only a procedural fragment shader: use ak-shader.
3D inside a Remotion video: use ak-remotion.
A design-led landing page with light 3D: use ak-frontend-design.

params.name: [3D scene or feature]
params.desc: 3D scene or feature to build (e.g. configurator, particles, XR).

examples.cmd: /ak:threejs product configurator for shoes with material color switching

tips: Always dispose GPU resources on unmount.
Use instancing, LOD, and batching for scenes with many objects.

ak-shader.tagline: Write GLSL fragment shaders: SDF shapes, noise, fBm, patterns.
ak-shader.summary: ak:shader writes GPU fragment shaders for procedural textures, distance-field shapes, patterns, noise, and animated effects. Output is GLSL for the target renderer (WebGL, Three.js, Processing), compiled and visually checked.
howItWorks: Inspects renderer, GLSL version, precision, and uniform names; samples are GLSL ES 1.
Loads only needed references (SDF, noise, fBm, patterns) and uses u_time, u_resolution, u_mouse.
Compiles and renders in the target and checks the image; syntax validation alone is not enough.
useWhen: Creating procedural textures such as wood, marble, clouds, or terrain.
Drawing SDF shapes or generating Perlin/simplex/cellular noise and fBm.
Writing custom shaders for Three.js materials or WebGL backgrounds.
avoidWhen: A full 3D scene with models, cameras, and lights: use ak-threejs.
Simple CSS effects or UI animation: use ak-frontend-design.
Offline image/video processing: use ak-media-processing.

params.name: [effect or pattern]
params.desc: Effect or pattern to create (e.g. marble texture, voronoi, wave animation).

tips: Sandboxes: editor.thebookofshaders.com, glslViewer, ShaderToy (uses iTime/iResolution instead of u_*).
Mind GLSL ES 1 (gl_FragColor) vs ES 3 (out vec4) for WebGL2/Three.js.
Many-octave noise is heavy on weak devices; measure performance.

ak-design.tagline: Brand identity and visual assets: logos, CIP, slides, banners, posters, icons.
ak-design.summary: ak:design owns art direction and visual deliverables (logos, CIP mockups, slides, banners, posters, social images, icons), checked at export. UI code belongs to frontend-design, frontend-development, and ui-styling.
howItWorks: Settles brief, audience, brand assets, format, and acceptance; asks only about missing key decisions.
For a real named brand, follows brand-asset-protocol.md and never invents its logo.
Loads the deliverable reference and runs scripts under scripts/logo, cip, icon, or poster.
Reviews with design-critique-guide.md and checks exports for clipping, resolution, and fidelity.
useWhen: Designing or revising a logo within brand constraints.
Creating a corporate identity program: cards, signage, uniforms, packaging.
Making posters, platform-sized banners, social images, or SVG icon sets.
avoidWhen: React/Tailwind UI code: use ak-frontend-design, ak-frontend-development, or ak-ui-styling.
Only concept/mockup images from curated prompts: use ak-ai-artist.

params.name: [design-type]
params.desc: Deliverable: logo, CIP, slides, banner, poster, social image, icons.

params.name: [context]
params.desc: Brief, audience, brand assets, format, and acceptance criteria.

examples.cmd: /ak:design CIP for a vintage coffee shop
examples.note: Identity mockups plus an HTML presentation.

examples.cmd: /ak:design LinkedIn banner for a product launch

tips: Image scripts use Gemini (Nano Banana) and need a Gemini API key.
Logos render on white backgrounds for easy extraction.
The Handoff Gate in references/handoff-gate.md is shared with frontend-design, show-off, and slides.

ak-ai-artist.tagline: Generate mockups, marketing assets, and concept art from 129 curated prompts.
ak-ai-artist.summary: ak:ai-artist matches your concept to 129 curated Nano Banana prompts and renders through ai-multimodal via Google or OpenRouter. It asks only when an unclear choice would change the image significantly.
howItWorks: Resolves concept, size, and brand constraints; a complete brief goes straight to generation.
Finds prompts with BM25 search over data/awesome-prompts.csv.
Runs python3 scripts/generate.py "<concept>" -o <output.png> with the chosen mode, provider, and model.
search uses the best prompt, creative blends the top 3, wild applies a random style, all does all three.
useWhen: Conference banners, thumbnails, or quote cards for social media.
Product shots, e-commerce mockups, or infographic-style concept art.
Several creative variants of one concept (--mode all).
avoidWhen: Logo, CIP, or brand system: use ak-design.
Image analysis, OCR, or video/audio generation: use ak-ai-multimodal.
Editing existing images: use ak-media-processing.

params.name: [concept]
params.desc: Idea or subject of the image.

params.name: --mode search|creative|wild|all
params.desc: search (default): best prompt; creative: blend top 3; wild: random artistic transform; all: all three. Script uses -m/--mode.

params.name: --provider auto|google|openrouter
params.desc: auto (default) honors IMAGE_GEN_PROVIDER=openrouter, else prefers Google; google or openrouter forces a provider.

params.name: --skip
params.desc: Skip the optional clarification and generate with stated assumptions.

params.name: -o, --output
params.desc: Output path (required).

params.name: -ar, --aspect-ratio
params.desc: Aspect ratio such as 1:1, 16:9, 9:16.

params.name: --model
params.desc: flash2 (default, fast), flash (previous), pro (quality/4K, slower and pricier).

params.name: -v, --verbose
params.desc: Show the matched prompt and details.

params.name: --dry-run
params.desc: Show the prompt only; no generation.

examples.note: Preview the prompt before spending quota.

tips: Needs GEMINI_API_KEY or OPENROUTER_API_KEY.
Use --dry-run to check the prompt before paying for generation.
Browse prompts with python3 scripts/search.py "<query>" --domain awesome.
artifacts: Image file at the -o path; several with --mode all

ak-ai-multimodal.tagline: Analyze and generate images, audio, video, documents; native vision first.
ak-ai-multimodal.summary: ak:ai-multimodal uses the session model's native vision for image/document understanding. It calls the @mrgoonie/multix CLI only when native vision cannot handle the input, or for generation, TTS, music, and transcription with a configured provider.
howItWorks: Routes understanding to native vision; generation and audio go to Multix if a matching key exists.
Falls back to Multix for analysis only when vision is missing, input exceeds limits, or you ask.
Checks GEMINI_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or MINIMAX_API_KEY presence; names the blocker when no route exists.
Runs multix --help on npm latest and picks an explicit model from the live provider catalog.
Splits oversized media with ffmpeg; transcripts are Markdown with [HH:MM:SS -> HH:MM:SS] lines.
useWhen: Transcribing long audio/video into a timestamped transcript.
Generating or editing images, short videos, music, or TTS.
Analyzing videos or documents beyond native vision limits.
avoidWhen: The current model can read the image/document itself: no Multix call needed.
Curated marketing image prompts: use ak-ai-artist.
Converting or encoding media: use ak-media-processing.

params.name: [file-path]
params.desc: Input media/document path, or the output target when generating.

params.name: [prompt]
params.desc: Analysis request or description of what to generate.

examples.note: Long video beyond native vision limits.

tips: Runs Multix via npx @mrgoonie/multix@latest; never a global install. Needs Node.js 20+.
Put keys in the shell, project .env, or ~/.multix/.env; one modality's key does not cover another.
Never assume a 'latest' model; check the current provider catalog.

ak-media-processing.tagline: Process media with FFmpeg, ImageMagick, and RMBG background removal.
ak-media-processing.summary: ak:media-processing encodes, converts, filters, resizes, makes thumbnails/GIFs, packages HLS/DASH, and removes backgrounds via CLI tools. It writes to a separate folder, keeps sources, and verifies output metadata.
howItWorks: Picks the tool: FFmpeg for video/audio, ImageMagick for images, RMBG for local AI background removal.
Loads encoding, streaming, filter, batch, or troubleshooting references as needed.
Runs commands or helper scripts (media_convert.py, video_optimize.py, batch_resize.py, remove-background.sh).
Writes to a separate folder, keeps sources, then verifies codec, size, duration, or metadata.
useWhen: Converting or compressing video, or extracting audio, thumbnails, and GIFs.
Batch resizing or converting images, or removing product photo backgrounds.
Packaging HLS/DASH streams.
avoidWhen: Generating new images/video with AI: use ak-ai-multimodal or ak-ai-artist.
Video from React code or HTML compositions: use ak-remotion or ak-hyperframes.
Transcribing audio: use ak-ai-multimodal.

params.name: [input-file]
params.desc: Input media file or set of files for batch jobs.

params.name: [operation]
params.desc: Operation: convert, encode, extract audio, resize, thumbnail, GIF, remove background, HLS/DASH.

examples.cmd: /ak:media-processing input.avi convert to mp4 H.264 crf 22

examples.note: ImageMagick batch into a separate folder.

tips: Needs ffmpeg, imagemagick (magick), and rmbg-cli installed.
mogrify overwrites in place; use it only when overwriting is allowed.
Lower CRF means higher quality; RMBG -m briaai is quality, -m u2netp is speed.
artifacts: Processed media (MP4, M4A, JPG/PNG, GIF, HLS/DASH) in a separate folder

ak-remotion.tagline: Make videos in React with Remotion: animation, captions, data-driven renders.
ak-remotion.summary: ak:remotion provides topic rules for Remotion code: animation, sequencing, transitions, audio, captions, fonts, charts, 3D, and more. Output is composition code and, on request, a rendered and checked video file.
howItWorks: Reads only the rules/ files matching the change (e.g. rules/animations.md).
Implements compositions and verifies ID, props, dimensions, fps, duration, assets, and audio sync.
For export, runs the installed render command and checks the file; a preview is not proof.
useWhen: Data-driven videos (animated charts, stats) from React code.
TikTok-style captions, .srt import, or audio transcription.
Intro/explainer videos with transitions, text animation, and music.
avoidWhen: Plain HTML/CSS compositions with data-* timing: use ak-hyperframes.
Only encoding, trimming, or format conversion: use ak-media-processing.

params.name: [video or component]
params.desc: Remotion video or component to create or edit.

examples.cmd: /ak:remotion 30-second quarterly revenue recap with animated charts
/ak:remotion render the Promo composition to MP4

tips: Load only the rules for the change at hand.
A Studio preview does not prove a successful render; check the output file.
Load fonts per rules/fonts.md to avoid render flicker.
artifacts: Rendered video file when export is requested

ak-hyperframes.tagline: Render videos from HTML compositions with HeyGen's HyperFrames CLI.
ak-hyperframes.summary: ak:hyperframes wraps the hyperframes CLI, run via npx at pinned hyperframes@0.7.99, to render plain-HTML compositions timed with data-* attributes. Output is a local MP4 (or cloud render with HEYGEN_API_KEY), done only when ffprobe confirms it.
howItWorks: Checks Node.js 22+ and FFmpeg with node scripts/verify-prereqs.mjs; prints READY or fix commands.
init scaffolds a project; you edit HTML with data-composition-id, data-start, data-duration, and class="clip".
preview serves a scrubbable timeline; lint always runs and must pass before render.
render outputs MP4 locally; cloud render is a separate command needing HEYGEN_API_KEY.
Verifies with ffprobe (non-zero duration, matching size); reports version drift from the pin, never upgrades silently.
useWhen: Short vertical social videos (1080x1920) built from HTML/CSS.
Launch clips, promo loops, or motion graphics authored as HTML.
You need HeyGen cloud rendering or distributed rendering on AWS/GCP.
avoidWhen: React components, frame-exact interpolation, or Remotion captions: use ak-remotion.
Only encoding, trimming, or transcoding: use ak-media-processing.
Static HTML previews or slides with no MP4: use ak-preview or ak-show-off.

params.name: [composition or command]
params.desc: Composition name/path or HyperFrames command (init, preview, lint, render, cloud render).

params.name: init
params.desc: Scaffold a composition project, e.g. init my-composition --resolution portrait; check init --help for current flags.

params.name: --resolution <preset>
params.desc: init: landscape (1920x1080), portrait (1080x1920), square (1080x1080), plus -4k variants and aliases like 1080p, 4k.

params.name: preview
params.desc: Serve the composition locally with a scrubbable timeline.

params.name: lint
params.desc: Check data-* attributes and timing; must pass before render.

params.name: render
params.desc: Render MP4 locally (Chromium capture + FFmpeg) with --output; no HEYGEN_API_KEY needed.

params.name: --output <path>
params.desc: MP4 output path for render and cloud render, e.g. ./assets/videos/<name>.mp4.

params.name: cloud render
params.desc: Render on HeyGen cloud; separate command, needs HEYGEN_API_KEY. cloud list/get/delete manage past renders.

params.name: lambda / cloudrun

ak-agent-browser.tagline: Automate tool-managed browsers: snapshots, clicks, forms, screenshots, QA.
ak-agent-browser.summary: ak:agent-browser drives Chrome/Chromium over CDP with the agent-browser CLI, using accessibility snapshots and @eN element refs. Real instructions come from the installed binary via agent-browser skills get core.
howItWorks: Routes tasks needing your real Chrome profile to ak:chrome-profile; everything else stays here.
Loads workflow content with agent-browser skills get core, or specialized skills (electron, slack, dogfood).
Opens the page, snapshots (-i) for @eN refs, clicks, fills forms, and screenshots.
Re-runs snapshot after every page change; cloud browsers use -p browserbase.
useWhen: Checking a freshly built page or taking screenshots.
Filling forms, scraping, or exploratory QA without real sign-in.
Automating Electron apps or running browsers in CI via Browserbase.
avoidWhen: You need cookies or accounts from your everyday Chrome: use ak-chrome-profile.
Repeatable E2E tests in CI: use ak-web-testing or Playwright.
OS-level control of native windows: use the computer-use skill.

params.name: [url or task]
params.desc: URL to open or description of the browser task.

examples.cmd: /ak:agent-browser dogfood the staging app to find bugs

tips: Install with npm install -g agent-browser; missing Chromium: agent-browser install --with-deps.
'Element not found': rerun agent-browser snapshot -i after the page changes.
Unknown flags: update the binary, then rerun agent-browser skills get core --full.

ak-chrome-profile.tagline: Automate your real Chrome profile via Chrome DevTools MCP.
ak-chrome-profile.summary: ak:chrome-profile opens a URL in an exact Chrome profile (account, cookies, tenant) and tags it with a #cdp-profile=<key>&cdp-open=<token> marker. The agent then binds that exact tab through Chrome DevTools MCP; it is not for ordinary browser testing.
howItWorks: Uses ak:agent-browser or ak:web-testing instead when the real profile is not needed.
Checks readiness: chrome-profile list resolves the key and a live MCP probe can read pages.
Runs chrome-profile setup for missing mappings, or doctor plus a live probe for bridge problems.
Opens with chrome-profile open --json <key> <url> and binds the tab whose URL has the exact token.
Never creates profile tabs with MCP new_page or navigate_page.
useWhen: Working in GitHub, Gmail, or Google Workspace with the signed-in account.
Several Chrome profiles exist and one must be targeted exactly.
The task needs cookies or a tenant from everyday Chrome.
avoidWhen: A fresh tool-managed browser is enough: use ak-agent-browser.
Repeatable CI tests: use ak-web-testing or Playwright.
Non-Chrome-stable browsers: the CLI does not support them.

params.name: [url]
params.desc: URL to open in the target profile.

params.name: --profile <name>
params.desc: Profile key, resolved by account email or display-name substring; never a folder name like 'Profile 17'.

params.name: --tab <title|url>
params.desc: Select a tab by title or URL. Not in source; bind via the cdp-open=<token> bind_selector instead.

params.name: open
params.desc: open <key> <url>: --json prints bind data; --force skips bridge check; --no-activate (macOS) keeps focus; --show-emails shows emails.

params.name: setup
params.desc: Discover profiles and write profiles.json; --yes accepts inferred keys, --non-interactive.

params.name: list
params.desc: Show configured keys and their resolved profiles.

params.name: discover
params.desc: List every Chrome profile on the machine; no config needed.

params.name: doctor
params.desc: Static check of whether tabs are readable; --json for bridge status. Always pair with a live MCP probe.

examples.note: View PRs with the work account.

tips: Requires Python 3.9+ and Google Chrome stable.
The first MCP call may show Chrome's remote-control dialog; approve it, then retry once.
The CLI reads only Local State metadata, never cookies or passwords.
